cards.title: Two-Species Allometric Scaling Methods
cards.claim: New two-species methods were developed as CL(human) = a(rat-dog) * W(human)^0.628 (rat-dog method) and CL(human) = a(rat-monkey) * W(human)^0.650 (rat-monkey method), where 'a' is the coefficient obtained allometrically from the corresponding two species. These methods showed predictive performance comparable to three-species-based Rule of Exponents (ROE).
conditions: Requires CL data from two specific species pairs (rat+dog or rat+monkey).
Exponents (0.628 and 0.650) are fixed for these specific methods.
Applicable when two-species data is available but three-species data is not.
required_inputs: CL data from rat and dog, OR rat and monkey.
Allometric coefficient 'a' derived from the two animal species.
limitations: Fixed exponents may not apply to all compounds.
Abstract does not detail how 'a' is calculated beyond 'obtained allometrically'.
Performance is 'comparable' to ROE, not necessarily superior in all cases.
cards.downstream_use: Implement as alternative translation methods when only two species are available, potentially reducing data requirements compared to standard ROE.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
